definitions.explanation: A wish or prayer, especially one made at a shrine, temple, or during a special occasion like Tanabata (Star Festival). Conveys a heartfelt or earnest desire, often directed to a higher power or the universe.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}で{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}をした。
examples.english: I made a wish at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {七夕|たなばた}に{短冊|たんざく}に{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote my wish on a strip of paper for Tanabata.

examples.japanese: {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}を{見|み}たら{三回|さんかい}{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}を{唱|とな}えると{叶|かな}うと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that if you see a shooting star and say your wish three times, it will come true.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{願|ねが}い{事|ごと} is closely associated with shrine and temple visits, especially at {初詣|はつもうで} (New Year's shrine visit) and during {七夕|たなばた} (Star Festival, July 7), when people write wishes on {短冊|たんざく} (paper strips) and hang them on bamboo.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {願|ねが}い{事|ごと}をする (to make a wish)
- {願|ねが}い{事|ごと}が{叶|かな}う (a wish comes true)
- {願|ねが}い{事|ごと}を{書|か}く (to write a wish)
- {願|ねが}い{事|ごと}を{唱|とな}える (to say/recite a wish)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {願|ねが}い{事|ごと}: wish (heartfelt, often spiritual/festive)
- {望|のぞ}み: hope, wish (broader, more general)
- {祈|いの}り: prayer (more religious or solemn)
- お{願|ねが}い: request, favor (directed at a person)
